nuggets.title: Hand-Edited Production Service Drifts from Golden Template

scenario.symptoms: On-call cannot reproduce payments-service prod config from the standard template. Missing metrics sidecar and wrong autoscaling limits caused a 2-hour outage.
scenario.interviewerSetup: An engineer hot-fixed production YAML six months ago; changes were never backported to the scaffold template. New deploys from template overwrite critical prod-only patches unpredictably.

incident.headline: Production services diverge from templates, causing fragile redeploys and missing platform defaults

agenda.goal: Keep services aligned with versioned golden templates via codegen, lint, and required override files.
agenda.opener: Prod payments-service no longer matches our standard template and the next deploy might drop the metrics sidecar. How do templates stay the source of truth?

evidence.strong: Versioned templates, codegen on create, CI diff against golden path, allowed extension points, automated backport bot, template upgrade runbooks.
evidence.adequate: Copy-paste template once at create with no drift checks.
evidence.weak: Every team writes YAML from scratch.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes scaffolding once at repo creation is enough.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens when the platform adds mandatory security sidecars six months later?

probes: How do teams customize without forking the whole template?
How are template version upgrades rolled out?
hints: Separate platform defaults from service-specific knobs.
CI should fail on unexpected diffs.
agenda.referenceFix: Golden templates with semver, generated base + owned overlay, CI policy gates on drift.

nuggets.title: Emergency SSH Escape Hatch Bypasses All Guardrails

scenario.symptoms: A Sev-1 fix required kubectl exec into production as root, disabling network policy and exporting customer data to a laptop. Post-incident review finds no approval trail.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Platform guardrails block direct prod access by default, but a shared break-glass role with static credentials was circulated in chat.

incident.headline: Unaudited break-glass access circumvents platform safety controls during incident response

agenda.goal: Provide time-bound, approved escape hatches with full audit and automatic expiry.
agenda.opener: During the outage someone used a shared break-glass account and turned off network policy. How should emergency access work on your platform?

evidence.strong: Just-in-time elevation with manager approval, max 1h TTL, session recorded, automatic revert, no static shared passwords, post-incident review required.
evidence.adequate: Break-glass role exists but without time bounds.
evidence.weak: Permanent admin kubeconfig for all senior engineers.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes guardrails must be permanently removed for fast incident response.
misconceptions.challenge: Can you grant scoped access for one pod for 30 minutes with audit?

probes: Who approves break-glass and for how long?
What gets logged during a session?
agenda.referenceFix: Approved JIT break-glass, immutable audit stream, automatic policy restore.

nuggets.title: Deploy Pipeline Skips CPU Limit Policy Gate

scenario.symptoms: A new service deploys without CPU limits and starves neighboring pods on shared nodes. Noisy neighbor causes cluster-wide latency spike.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Admission controller policy requires limits, but the deploy pipeline used an emergency `--skip-policy` flag that was never removed from the template.

incident.headline: Policy guardrails bypassed in CI allow unbounded workloads onto shared infrastructure

agenda.goal: Enforce guardrails at admission and in CI with no silent bypass except audited break-glass.
agenda.opener: A deploy without CPU limits took down neighbors on the node pool. What guardrails should have blocked it?

evidence.strong: OPA/Gatekeeper policies on limits, probes, labels; CI renders manifests and fails on violation; no permanent skip flags; periodic audit of live cluster vs policy.
evidence.adequate: Documentation says set limits but no enforcement.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes written standards replace automated enforcement.

probes: Where are policies enforced: CI, admission, or both?
hints: Admission is the last line of defense.
agenda.referenceFix: Mandatory policy checks in CI and admission, exception workflow with expiry.

nuggets.title: Shared Terraform State Blocks All Service Provisioning

scenario.symptoms: Fifty teams queue on a single Terraform state lock for the shared platform stack. A stuck apply from yesterday prevents any new service onboarding.
scenario.interviewerSetup: All microservices share one monolithic state file in S3. One engineer's local apply crashed after acquiring the lock.

incident.headline: Monolithic IaC state creates global lock contention and blocks independent service provisioning

agenda.goal: Split IaC into scoped state per service or domain with automated pipelines and lock timeout hygiene.
agenda.opener: Onboarding froze because one Terraform lock never released. How is infrastructure code organized for hundreds of services?

evidence.strong: State per service or domain, remote runs in CI only, lock force with audit, module library, blast-radius limited stacks.
evidence.adequate: Single state with manual lock break.

misconceptions.pattern: Prefers one state file to see everything.
misconceptions.challenge: What happens when two teams apply unrelated changes simultaneously?

probes: How big should a Terraform state be?
Who is allowed to run apply locally?
agenda.referenceFix: Sharded Terraform state, pipeline-only apply, stale lock automation.

nuggets.title: Critical CVE in Shared Base Image Hits Every Service

scenario.symptoms: Scanner flags CVE-2024-XXXX in OpenSSL across 400 services. Only 12% rebuilt images after the platform team published a patched base tag two weeks ago.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Services pin `platform-base:2024.01` without auto-rebuild. No policy blocks deploy of images older than N days.

incident.headline: Stale base image pins leave fleet exposed after centralized patch release

agenda.goal: Roll out base image CVE fixes with rebuild automation, deploy deadlines, and admission deny on critical CVEs.
agenda.opener: A critical OpenSSL CVE is in our shared base and most services never rebuilt. How does the platform drive fleet-wide patching?

evidence.strong: Automated rebuild on new base tag, SBOM tracking, policy blocking critical CVEs at admission, dashboard of lagging services, canary base rollout.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes app code changes are required to pick up OS patches.
misconceptions.challenge: If only the base layer changed, what triggers a new deploy?

probes: How do you know which running pods are still vulnerable?
hints: Central base image with semver tags.
agenda.referenceFix: Automated downstream rebuilds on base publish, admission deny list for critical CVEs.
